issue_context.title: Iterating large queue throws exception
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-collections See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Description Iterating large queue throw exception. ### Reproduction Steps ``` using System.Collections.Generic; using System; var queue = new Queue < int > (); queue.EnsureCapacity(Array.MaxLength); for (var i = 0; i < Array.MaxLength - 2; i++) { queue.Enqueue(i); queue.Dequeue(); } for (var i = 0; i < Int32.MaxValue - Array.MaxLength + 4; i++) { queue.Enqueue(i); } var latest = 0; foreach(var i in queue) { latest = i; } Console.WriteLine(latest); ``` ### Expected behavior Do not throws exception. ### Actual behavior ``` Unhandled exception. System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array. at System.Collections.Generic.Queue`1.Enumerator.MoveNext() ``` ### Regression? _No response_ ### Known Workarounds _No response_ ### Configuration _No response_ ### Other information _No response_
Author: AkiSakurai
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Collections`
Milestone: -

`foreach(var i in queue) {` line is throwing the exception (during `MoveNext`).

This expression overflows: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/6b170de3428356845261b0f025ed9153aa293f47/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Collections/Generic/Queue.cs#L465 `arrayIndex` becomes `-2147483648` on iterating the last (59<sup>th</sup>) index.

Current workaround is to call `ToArray()`, as in: `foreach(var i in queue.ToArray()) {` which  will make a copy of underlying storage (it's horrible, but better than being blocked 🙂).

> Regression?

No. This issue is also present in .NET 6.
